ing: catfish, cod or snapper, cut into bite-size pieces
st: Blend the lemongrass, galangal, 2 lime leaves, garlic, shallots, soaked chilies, turmeric and [[2 tbsp]] of the coconut milk into a smooth paste.
In a bowl, mix the paste with [[1 cup]] coconut milk, the eggs, fish sauce and sugar until smooth. This is the curry custard.
Fold in the fish pieces so each is coated. Let it marinate for 15 minutes.
Line four heatproof bowls with cabbage leaves, then divide the fish and curry mixture among them.
Set up a steamer with simmering water. Steam the bowls, covered, until the custard is just set and the fish is opaque.
Meanwhile, warm the remaining [[0.5 cup]] coconut milk with a pinch of salt for the topping.
Spoon the warm coconut milk on top and scatter with the shredded lime leaves. Serve with steamed rice.
Mix the beef with the soy sauce, oyster sauce, garlic, sugar, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and [[1 tbsp]] oil. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Make the dipping sauce: stir the juice of 2 limes, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and [[0.5 tsp]] salt together in a small bowl.
Arrange the lettuce, tomatoes and onion on a platter.
Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat until smoking. Add [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Add half the beef in a single layer and sear without moving for 1 minute, then stir-fry until browned outside and slightly pink inside, about 3 minutes.
Remove the beef and repeat with the remaining oil and beef.
Spoon the beef over the lettuce and serve with rice and the lime-pepper dip.
Put the bones in a pot, cover with [[4 cups]] water and boil for 5 minutes. Drain, rinse the bones and clean the pot.
Return the bones to the pot with [[8 cups]] fresh water and the halved onion. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently, partly covered.
Season the broth with fish sauce, sugar and salt. Strain out the bones and onion.
Heat the oil in a small pan over low heat and cook the garlic until pale golden, about 2 minutes. Set aside.
Soak the rice noodles in warm water for 20 minutes or as the package says, then boil 1 minute and drain.
Bring the broth to a rolling boil. Poach the pork slices and shrimp in it for 2 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and the pork is cooked through.
Divide the noodles, pork, shrimp and bean sprouts among bowls. Ladle hot broth over.
Top with the garlic oil and scallions and serve with lime wedges.

ing: tilapia or catfish, cut into chunks
st: Boil the fish in [[3 cups]] water for 8 minutes until cooked through. Lift out the fish and keep the cooking water.
Flake the fish into pieces, removing any bones.
Blend the lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, garlic, turmeric and the fish with a ladle of the cooking water into a paste.
Pour the paste back into the cooking water and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring.
Stir in the coconut milk and fish sauce and simmer 5 more minutes. This is the green curry gravy.
Cook the noodles according to the package (fresh need only a quick rinse in hot water). Drain.
Pile the noodles in bowls. Top with cucumber, bean sprouts and herbs and ladle the gravy over.
Mix the pork with the garlic, coconut milk, soy sauce, fish sauce, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and pepper. Marinate for at least 1 hour.
Make quick pickles: stir the vinegar, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and salt until dissolved, then pour over the carrots. Let them sit while you cook.
Cook the rice with [[3 cups]] water until tender.
Heat a grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat and brush with oil.
Cook the pork slices in a single layer for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through with no pink left.
Pile the rice on plates, lay the pork over it, and add cucumber and pickled vegetables.
Serve with a bowl of warm chicken broth or the pickle liquid on the side.

ing: fermented fish paste; or 1 tbsp anchovy paste plus 1 tbsp fish sauce
st: Toast the rice in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, until deep golden and fragrant, about 5 minutes. Grind it to a coarse powder in a spice grinder.
Heat the oil in a large pot. Fry the garlic and lemongrass for 1 minute, then add the pork and brown it for 5 minutes.
Stir in the prahok and cook for 2 minutes.
Add [[8 cups]] water, bring to a boil, then simmer the pork until just tender.
Add the pumpkin and papaya and cook 10 minutes.
Add the eggplant and green beans and cook until tender, about 8 minutes more.
Stir in the ground toasted rice and fish sauce and simmer 5 minutes to thicken. Taste and adjust. The pork should be cooked through to 145°F (63°C).
Serve hot over steamed rice.

ing: or any firm white fish, cut in chunks
or the pulp from soaked tamarind
st: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the garlic, shallot and lemongrass for 2 minutes.
Add [[6 cups]] water and bring to a boil.
Stir in the tamarind paste, fish sauce and sugar until dissolved.
Add the pineapple and tomatoes and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the fish chunks and celery and simmer gently until the fish is opaque and flaky.
Taste: it should be sour, sweet and salty. Adjust with more sugar, tamarind or fish sauce.
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve hot with rice.

ing: cleaned and cut into pieces, shells cracked
on the sprig; or 1 tbsp coarsely cracked black pepper
st: Rinse the crab pieces well and pat dry. Crack the claws lightly with the back of a knife so the flavors get inside.
Mix the oyster sauce, fish sauce, sugar and [[0.25 cup]] water in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a large wok over high heat. Add the garlic and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the green peppercorns and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the crab and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Pour in the sauce, cover and cook on medium-high until the shells are bright red or orange and the meat is opaque.
Toss in the scallions and cook 1 minute. Serve right away with rice and lime.

ing: fermented fish paste; or 1.5 tbsp anchovy paste plus 1 tbsp fish sauce
cucumber, cabbage and green beans, to serve
st: Pound or blend the lemongrass, chilies, garlic, shallots and turmeric into a rough paste.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the paste for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the prahok and cook, mashing it, for 2 minutes.
Add the pork and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F (71°C), about 8 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the sugar. Simmer gently, stirring, until thickened.
Add the eggplants and simmer 5 more minutes until soft.
Taste and adjust. Serve warm as a dip with raw vegetables and rice.
Whisk the [[1 cup]] rice flour, [[1 cup]] of the coconut milk, sugar, salt and cooked rice (if using) into a smooth, thin batter. Rest 15 minutes.
For the topping, whisk the remaining [[0.5 cup]] coconut milk, [[1 tbsp]] rice flour and a pinch of salt in a small bowl.
Heat a mold pan (like an aebleskiver or takoyaki pan) over medium-low heat and brush each hole with oil.
Fill each hole about two thirds full with the batter. Cover and cook for 2 minutes.
Spoon a little of the coconut topping on each and add a pinch of scallion.
Cover again and cook until the bottoms are crisp and golden and the tops are set, about 4 minutes.
Use a skewer to lift them out. Close pairs together like a ball, and serve warm.

ing: optional, halved lengthwise for sweet version
st: Soak the sticky rice and mung beans in separate bowls of cold water for 2 hours. Drain well.
Steam the mung beans for 15 minutes until soft, then mash lightly with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Toss the drained rice with the coconut milk, sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Season the pork with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Lay a banana leaf flat (warm it briefly over a flame to soften). Spread a layer of rice, a layer of mung bean mash, a strip of pork (or banana), then more rice on top.
Roll it up tightly into a log, fold the ends in and tie with string. Make the rest the same way.
Steam or simmer in plenty of water, covered, until the rice is tender and the pork is cooked through.
Cool for 10 minutes, unwrap and slice. Serve warm or at room temperature.
